claims.text: LLM hallucinations can be categorized into two primary types: factuality hallucination and faithfulness hallucination.
Factuality hallucination in LLMs encompasses factual contradiction and factual fabrication.
Faithfulness hallucination in LLMs encompasses instruction inconsistency, context inconsistency, and logical inconsistency.
Incorporating new factual knowledge during supervised fine-tuning correlates with increased hallucinations in LLMs.
Elevating the sampling temperature during decoding increases the risk of hallucinations by increasing the likelihood of sampling low-frequency tail tokens.
LLMs exhibit a logical reasoning failure known as the Reversal Curse where they fail at logical deduction when questions are inverted from 'A is B' to 'B is A'.

evidence.description: The authors state: 'We categorize hallucination into two primary types: factuality hallucination and faithfulness hallucination.'
The authors define factuality hallucination subcategories as: 'we categorize these factuality hallucinations into two primary types: Factual Contradiction... Factual Fabrication'.
The paper subdivides faithfulness hallucination: 'This category is further subdivided into instruction inconsistency... context inconsistency... and logical inconsistency.'

The paper cites findings by Gekhman et al.: 'they discovered a correlation between the acquisition of new knowledge through SFT and increased hallucinations, suggesting that introducing new factual knowledge encourages LLMs to hallucinate.'

The survey explains decoding impact: 'An elevation in the sampling temperature results in a more uniform token probability distribution, increasing the likelihood of sampling tokens with lower frequencies from the tail of the distribution. Consequently, this heightened tendency to sample infrequently occurring tokens exacerbates the risk of hallucinations'.

The paper references Berglund et al.: 'Berglund et al. [22] unveiled a specific reasoning failure in LLMs termed the Reversal Curse. Specifically, while the model can correctly answer when the question is formulated as "A is B", it exhibits a failed logical deduction when asked the converse "B is A".'

methodologies.name: LLM Hallucination Granular Taxonomy
methodologies.description: A hierarchical categorization framework dividing LLM hallucinations into factuality hallucinations (factual contradiction and factual fabrication) and faithfulness hallucinations (instruction, context, and logical inconsistency).

methodologies.name: Cause-Driven Mitigation Taxonomy
methodologies.description: A structured taxonomy connecting hallucination mitigation techniques to root causes across data, training, and inference stages.
conditions: Survey and analysis of LLM hallucination literature

limitations.text: Prior task-specific hallucination taxonomies fail to capture open-ended, general-purpose LLM interactions and factual error complexities.
Current Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems remain vulnerable to hallucinations caused by retrieval failures, noisy contexts, knowledge conflicts, and generation bottlenecks.
Relying exclusively on an LLM's parametric knowledge for internal fact-checking is prone to inaccurate assessments because LLMs are not inherently reliable factual databases.

future_work.text: Investigating multi-modal hallucinations in Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs), including perception errors, multi-image contextual misalignments, and logical reasoning flaws.
Developing reliable probing methods to accurately understand internal knowledge boundaries and internal belief structures in LLMs to prevent overconfident generation of unanswerable queries.
